_source: Hand-located by eye on out/working_a.png (3024x4032) against the drawn state outline; each seed was visually confirmed to sit on the boundary rule itself, not on a label, locality number, road, river, or lake edge. These are raw hand-placed seeds and are never refined.
_role: These seeds only bracket the six boundary edges -- each adjacent pair says roughly where one edge runs so perimeter.trace_edge knows which way to walk and which way to search. They must not influence the traced result: perimeter.py traces each drawn rule along its length and solves each corner from the arcs of the two edges meeting there, and the corners it returns are insensitive to seed placement (measured at 0.49-0.55 px under +/-10 px seed jitter). Do not treat these as corner estimates. The earlier straight-line edge fitting these seeds were first written for is gone; see README 'Superseded' and do not reintroduce it.
_warning: Local corner refinement was tried and abandoned. Three corners have non-boundary ink inside any usable window (n_notch: the label '27'; notch_inner: '30', 'Anschutz' and the I-80 shield, which also occlude the 41st-parallel rule east of the corner; sw: '103 Beaver Dam' plus the book-gutter shadow). The old corners.refine_corner fitted that ink and returned a wrong point without raising -- up to 1119 px (~222 km) under seed jitter -- and has been deleted. See README 'Superseded'.
